days.gratitude: A morning sound that told me the day had started.
days.intention: Before noon, I'll finish one thing I keep circling.
days.higher_self: What do you want me to say to you first thing tomorrow?
days.shadow: Where did I say "I'm fine" today when I wasn't quite?
days.humor: December has arrived. Rank my holiday prep: none / a list / a list about the list.
days.meditation: Sit tall and let your hands rest open. Breathe in through the nose for a slow count of four, and out for six. Picture the first light of morning on a windowsill. With each breath in, say silently, "I am listening." With each breath out, "I am heard." Let your shoulders drop a little lower each round. Do this six times. Before you open your eyes, name one thing you would like to bring before God today, and hold it there gently, like a cup in both hands.
days.verse: My voice shalt thou hear in the morning, O LORD; in the morning will I direct my prayer unto thee, and will look up.
days.faith_reflection: What would change if I spoke to God before I spoke to my phone?
days.faith_action: Tomorrow, say one sentence of prayer before you check a screen.

days.gratitude: A path I walk often that I've stopped noticing.
days.intention: Today I'll follow the joy, even if it's small.
days.higher_self: Which direction feels warmer right now?
days.shadow: What joy do I talk myself out of because it feels silly?
days.humor: A sign from the universe I ignored because I was looking at my phone.
days.meditation: Close your eyes and picture a winding path through a winter field. Your feet are warm. Take a slow step with each breath. On the in-breath, notice something along the path: a stone, a branch, a bird. On the out-breath, keep walking. After eight steps, the path opens into a clearing filled with soft light. Stand there. Let the light rest on your face. Whisper, "Show me the way." Wait in the quiet a moment, then walk back slowly, carrying the warmth with you.
days.verse: Thou wilt shew me the path of life: in thy presence is fulness of joy; at thy right hand there are pleasures for evermore.
days.faith_reflection: Where have I already felt "fulness of joy" this week?
days.faith_action: Write down one joyful moment as soon as it happens today.

days.gratitude: Someone who was patient with me.
days.intention: Today I'll wait well instead of waiting worried.
days.higher_self: What are you asking me to be patient about?
days.shadow: What do I do with my hands and mind when I hate waiting?
days.humor: Things I refreshed today hoping they'd change: ___ (tally marks welcome).
days.meditation: Settle in and set a soft timer for two minutes. Breathe naturally. Imagine you are sitting in a quiet waiting room, and you are not in a hurry. Each time a thought tugs at you to rush, picture setting it on the chair beside you. Say, "Not yet, and that is okay." Feel your heartbeat slow. Notice the strength in simply staying. When the timer sounds, take one deep breath, and say, "I can wait with courage." Then rise gently.
days.verse: Wait on the LORD: be of good courage, and he shall strengthen thine heart: wait, I say, on the LORD.
days.faith_reflection: What am I waiting on, and how can I wait with courage instead of dread?
days.faith_action: Name one waiting thing and pray about it once, then let it rest today.

days.gratitude: A flavor I enjoyed today and why.
days.intention: Today I'll taste my food and my moments.
days.higher_self: What goodness have I been too busy to taste?
days.shadow: Where do I eat, scroll, or shop to avoid feeling something?
days.humor: Foods I've called "a treat" this week vs. foods I've actually eaten. Discuss.
days.meditation: Hold something small to eat, a raisin, a square of chocolate, or a sip of tea. Look at it as if for the first time. Notice its color and texture. Breathe in its scent slowly. Take one small taste and let it rest on your tongue without chewing for a moment. Notice sweetness, warmth, or bitterness. Swallow slowly. Breathe in and say, "Taste." Breathe out and say, "and see." Let gratitude rise for the hands that grew, made, and brought this to you.
days.verse: O taste and see that the LORD is good: blessed is the man that trusteth in him.
days.faith_reflection: Where did I "taste and see" goodness today without expecting it?
days.faith_action: Eat one meal today with no screen and say thanks before the first bite.

days.gratitude: Something about how I'm made that I'm thankful for on my birthday.
days.intention: This year, I'll treat myself like someone I love.
days.higher_self: What do you see in me that I'm only starting to see?
days.shadow: What old label about myself am I ready to retire this year?
days.humor: Birthday wish list from my inner child vs. my inner accountant.
days.meditation: Place a hand over your heart and feel it beat. This heart has kept time for every year of your life. Breathe in slowly and count the years in tens, letting each decade appear as a picture: a face, a place, a song. Do not judge any of them. With each one, say, "Thank you for carrying me." Then picture the year ahead as an open door with light behind it. Take one breath at the threshold. Say, "I am wonderfully made," and step through.
days.verse: I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made: marvellous are thy works; and that my soul knoweth right well.
days.faith_reflection: Which part of me have I called a flaw that God might call marvellous?
days.faith_action: Write yourself one birthday sentence that starts, "I'm proud of you for…"

days.gratitude: Someone who helped me carry something this year.
days.intention: Today I'll set one burden down on purpose.
days.higher_self: What am I holding that was never mine to carry?
days.shadow: Whose problem have I adopted as if it were my job to fix?
days.humor: My emotional baggage, sorted by airline weight limits.
days.meditation: Picture a backpack on your shoulders. Feel its weight. One by one, name what is inside: a worry, a task, someone else's feelings. As you name each, imagine lifting it out and placing it on a large, steady stone in front of you. Breathe out each time. When the pack is lighter, slip it off and set it down too. Roll your shoulders. Breathe in, "I am sustained." Breathe out, "I don't carry this alone." Rest for three breaths before you pick back up only what is truly yours.
days.verse: Cast thy burden upon the LORD, and he shall sustain thee: he shall never suffer the righteous to be moved.
days.faith_reflection: What burden have I been praying about while still holding it tight?
days.faith_action: Write the burden on a scrap, pray once, and fold the paper away.

days.gratitude: A safe place I can always return to.
days.intention: Today I'll make one corner of my life feel sheltered.
days.higher_self: Where is my secret place with you?
days.shadow: When do I feel unsafe, and what does that younger part of me need?
days.humor: Places I've hidden from responsibilities: a ranking (the laundry room is undefeated).
days.meditation: Imagine a quiet room that only you and God know. Furnish it slowly: a soft chair, a window, a blanket, a lamp. Sit there in your mind. Breathe in for four, hold for two, breathe out for six. Hear the world muffled outside, as if under snow. Nothing is required of you here. Say, "I dwell in the secret place." Let your body sink into the chair. Stay for five more breaths. When you leave, know the door stays open and you can come back anytime.
days.verse: He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.
days.faith_reflection: Where is my "secret place," and how often do I visit it?
days.faith_action: Choose a two-minute spot today and sit there in silence once.

days.gratitude: A fresh start I was given that I didn't earn.
days.intention: At this New Moon, I plant one seed: ___.
days.higher_self: What new heart are you growing in me?
days.shadow: Where has my heart gone stony, and what made it that way?
days.humor: New Moon intentions I set last time that I've already forgotten. Be honest.
days.meditation: The moon is dark tonight, a resting dark, before the light returns. Close your eyes and picture holding a single seed in your palm. Breathe on it gently. With each breath in, name one quality you want to grow: patience, courage, joy. With each breath out, picture pressing the seed into soft, dark soil. Cover it carefully. Say, "A new heart, a new spirit." Feel the hope of something unseen beginning. Rest your hands on your lap and trust the growing to God.
days.verse: A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh.
days.faith_reflection: What would a heart of flesh do differently in one relationship this month?
days.faith_action: Write the New Moon seed on the page and one tiny first step.

days.gratitude: A blessing from this week I almost forgot.
days.intention: Today I'll count benefits before I count problems.
days.higher_self: What have you done for me that I haven't noticed?
days.shadow: What do I complain about that someone else would pray for?
days.humor: Times I said "I'm so blessed" vs. times I said "ugh." Tally it.
days.meditation: Breathe in slowly and on each breath recall one good thing from the past seven days. Picture it clearly. A kind word, a warm meal, a laugh, a solved problem. On the out-breath say, "Thank you." Count them on your fingers as you go. When you reach ten, place both hands flat on your legs and feel how full they are. Say, "Bless the Lord, O my soul." Let a small smile come if it wants to. Sit with the fullness for three slow breaths.
days.verse: Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits:
days.faith_reflection: Which of God's benefits do I tend to forget first?
days.faith_action: List five benefits from today before bed.

days.gratitude: A view that lifts my mood.
days.intention: Today I'll look up more than I look down.
days.higher_self: Where do I look for help before I look to you?
days.shadow: Who do I go to for approval when I should go to myself or to God?
days.humor: Things I looked up today: the weather 4 times, the hills 0 times.
days.meditation: Sit near a window if you can. Lift your chin slightly and soften your gaze upward, toward the sky or the ceiling. Breathe in and imagine broad hills in the distance, steady and old. Breathe out and feel your feet on the ground. Let your eyes rest high while your body rests low. Say, "My help comes from the Lord." Repeat it slowly three times. Notice any tightness in your jaw or brow and let it melt. Return your gaze to the room with a calm heart.
days.verse: I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help.
days.faith_reflection: Where am I looking for help right now, and is it the right place?
days.faith_action: Step outside or to a window and look up for one full minute.

days.gratitude: A healing I've seen in myself or someone I love.
days.intention: Today I'll be gentle with a sore spot.
days.higher_self: What wound are you quietly binding up?
days.shadow: Which old hurt still flinches when someone touches it?
days.humor: My body's check-engine lights, ranked by how long I've ignored each.
days.meditation: Find a comfortable position and close your eyes. Breathe in through the nose, out through the mouth. Notice a place in your body or heart that feels tender. Do not fix it. Just place your attention there like a warm hand. Imagine a soft bandage of light wrapping it gently. Breathe in, "He heals." Breathe out, "He binds." Stay with this for six breaths. If tears come, let them. If nothing comes, that is fine too. Finish by thanking your body for working so hard to mend.
days.verse: He healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds.
days.faith_reflection: What brokenness am I ready to bring to God, even just a little?
days.faith_action: Do one caring thing for a sore spot: rest, a call, a walk, a note.

days.gratitude: The last thing that made me laugh out loud.
days.intention: Today I'll let myself be delighted.
days.higher_self: What makes you laugh about me (kindly)?
days.shadow: When do I hold back laughter because I'm afraid I'll look silly?
days.humor: My most "awakened" moment this week turned out to be... a nap.
days.meditation: Sit comfortably and let a small smile rest on your face, even if it feels forced. Notice how your cheeks lift and your eyes soften. Breathe in and recall a moment you laughed so hard you couldn't stop. Picture who was there. Breathe out and let your belly loosen. Do this five times, each time picturing a different laugh. Say, "A merry heart is good medicine." Let your smile stay as you open your eyes. Notice if the room feels lighter.
days.verse: A merry heart doeth good like a medicine: but a broken spirit drieth the bones.
days.faith_reflection: Where could I take my faith a little less grimly today?
days.faith_action: Send someone a joke or a funny memory today.

days.gratitude: Someone who answered me softly when I was sharp.
days.intention: Today I'll choose the softer answer once.
days.higher_self: What would a soft answer sound like in my hardest conversation?
days.shadow: What triggers my sharp tone, and what is the hurt underneath it?
days.humor: My inner monologue during holiday traffic, rated PG-13.
days.meditation: Take a deep breath and notice your tongue resting in your mouth. Let it soften. Unclench your teeth. Breathe out slowly as if fogging a mirror. Picture a recent tense moment. Do not replay the words; just notice the heat in your body. On the next breath in, imagine cool air flowing to that heat. On the out-breath say, "Soft answer." Repeat six times. Picture yourself in the same moment, speaking slowly and kindly. Notice how it lands. Carry that gentleness into your next conversation.
days.verse: A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.
days.faith_reflection: Whose anger might I turn with a gentle word this week?
days.faith_action: Pause and breathe once before replying to anything that stings today.

days.gratitude: A time I cried that turned out to be healing.
days.intention: Today I'll let my feelings move instead of freezing them.
days.higher_self: Is this a season to weep, laugh, mourn, or dance for me?
days.shadow: Which feeling do I judge as "wrong" for this time of year?
days.humor: Holiday feelings bingo: nostalgic, overwhelmed, sugar crash, "why did I say yes."
days.meditation: Stand or sit and let your body sway very slightly, side to side, like a slow pendulum. Breathe naturally. Ask yourself, "What season am I in today?" Let the answer come as a single word. Do not argue with it. If it is sorrow, place a hand on your chest. If it is joy, let your sway become a small dance. Say, "There is a time for this." Breathe with whatever came. After a minute, become still and thank God that every season is held.
days.verse: A time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;
days.faith_reflection: Where have I refused a season because it didn't match my plans?
days.faith_action: Give your current feeling ten honest minutes today.

days.gratitude: A thought that steadied me this week.
days.intention: Today I'll keep my mind stayed on what is true.
days.higher_self: Where is my mind wandering that robs my peace?
days.shadow: What anxious story do I tell most often, and is it true?
days.humor: Number of open tabs in my browser vs. in my brain. Who's winning?
days.meditation: Breathe in for four and out for four. Imagine your mind as a lake on a windy day, full of ripples. With each out-breath, the wind calms a little. Watch the water slowly smooth. As it stills, a clear reflection of the sky appears. Say, "Perfect peace." When a thought ripples the water, notice it, then breathe it smooth again. Stay with the stillness for eight breaths. Remember that you can return to this lake whenever the wind picks up.
days.verse: Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee.
days.faith_reflection: What is my mind "stayed" on most today?
days.faith_action: Write one true, trustworthy thought on a card and read it at noon.

days.gratitude: A rest I took that I didn't feel guilty about.
days.intention: Today I'll find strength in quiet rather than hustle.
days.higher_self: What quiet thing do you want me to return to?
days.shadow: Where do I prove my worth through busyness?
days.humor: My to-do list vs. my "did-do" list. One of these is fiction.
days.meditation: Lie down or lean back comfortably. Let gravity hold you. Breathe in slowly and feel your back supported. Breathe out and let your arms grow heavy. Say, "In returning and rest." Picture yourself walking home after a long day, opening the door, and sitting down. No one needs anything from you right now. Breathe in, "quietness," breathe out, "confidence." Stay for ten breaths. Notice that rest is not weakness. It is where strength is refilled. Take one more slow breath, feel your feet on the floor, and when you are ready, open your eyes.
days.verse: For thus saith the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel; In returning and rest shall ye be saved; in quietness and in confidence shall be your strength: and ye would not.
days.faith_reflection: Where have I said "I would not" to rest God offered?
days.faith_action: Take ten unhurried minutes today with nothing to produce.

days.gratitude: Someone who showed me mercy without lecturing.
days.intention: Today I'll do one just thing, love one mercy, walk one humble step.
days.higher_self: What does walking humbly with you look like this week?
days.shadow: Where do I want to be right more than I want to be kind?
days.humor: My humble-brag of the week (and the real story behind it).
days.meditation: Begin walking slowly, indoors or out. If you cannot walk, imagine it. Match each step to a breath. Step one: "do justly." Step two: "love mercy." Step three: "walk humbly." Repeat this rhythm. Feel your heel, then your toes, touch the ground. Notice how humility feels in the body, not small, just honest and grounded. Keep walking for a minute or two. When you stop, stand still and say, "With my God." Take one deep breath and carry that steadiness into your day.
days.verse: He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?
days.faith_reflection: Which of the three (justice, mercy, humility) do I find hardest right now?
days.faith_action: Do one quiet act of mercy that no one will praise.

days.gratitude: A prayer that was answered in a way I didn't expect.
days.intention: Today I'll ask clearly for what I need.
days.higher_self: What do I want but haven't asked for?
days.shadow: Why do I feel I must earn the right to ask?
days.humor: Things I asked the universe for vs. things I asked Google for. Compare.
days.meditation: Sit with your palms facing up. Breathe in and picture a door in front of you. Breathe out and notice your hand reaching up to knock. Knock gently three times in your mind. With each knock, say one word of what you need: peace, wisdom, provision, anything. Wait. Breathe slowly. Imagine the door opening just a little and warm light spilling out. You do not need to see everything inside. Say, "Ask, seek, knock." Rest your hands and trust the answer is coming.
days.verse: Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you:
days.faith_reflection: What have I stopped asking for because I gave up?
days.faith_action: Write one honest ask on the page and pray it out loud.

days.gratitude: A peaceful moment that surprised me this month.
days.intention: Today I won't let my heart be troubled by what's not mine to solve.
days.higher_self: What kind of peace are you offering me that the world can't?
days.shadow: What do I let trouble my heart before it even happens?
days.humor: Worries I had this morning that already expired by lunch.
days.meditation: Breathe in and imagine receiving a gift. It is wrapped simply, no bow. Open it slowly in your mind. Inside is a soft glow of peace. Lift it out and hold it to your chest. Feel it spread through your ribs and shoulders. Breathe in, "Peace I leave." Breathe out, "My peace I give." Repeat six times. Notice what the world's peace feels like, usually rushed and conditional. Then notice this one, quiet and steady. Keep it close as you return to your day.
days.verse: Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.
days.faith_reflection: Where am I still trying to get peace the world's way?
days.faith_action: When worry comes today, say, "Let not your heart be troubled."

days.gratitude: A song that lifts me when I'm low.
days.intention: Today I'll remember that I am rejoiced over.
days.higher_self: What song would you sing over me today?
days.shadow: When do I feel unworthy of being celebrated?
days.humor: My shower-concert setlist this week, honestly reviewed.
days.meditation: Hum softly, any low note, for the length of one out-breath. Feel the vibration in your chest and throat. Breathe in. Hum again. Do this five times. Now imagine God humming over you the way a parent hums over a sleeping child. Let yourself be the one sung to. Say, "He rejoices over me with singing." Let your face soften. Stay in that picture for six quiet breaths. Then hum once more, as your answer back. Take one more slow breath, feel your feet on the floor, and when you are ready, open your eyes.
days.verse: The LORD thy God in the midst of thee is mighty; he will save, he will rejoice over thee with joy; he will rest in his love, he will joy over thee with singing.
days.faith_reflection: How would I live today if I truly believed God delights in me?
days.faith_action: Play one song today and let it be a prayer.

days.gratitude: A light that kept me going through a dark time.
days.intention: On this shortest day, I'll let one small light lead me.
days.higher_self: What light are you shining into my darkest corner?
days.shadow: What darkness am I scared to look at, even gently?
days.humor: Ways I survive the longest night: snacks, blankets, more snacks.
days.meditation: Today the sun reaches its winter turning point. Dim the lights if you can and light a candle or picture one. Watch the flame. Breathe in slowly and notice how even a tiny light changes a dark room. Breathe out and let your eyes soften. Say, "The light shines in darkness." Think of one hard place in your life and imagine the flame set right there. It doesn't fix everything. It just makes the room visible. Rest with the flame for eight breaths.
days.verse: And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not.
days.faith_reflection: Where has light kept shining even when I couldn't understand it?
days.faith_action: Light a candle or a lamp tonight and pray for someone in a dark season.

days.gratitude: One name of God that comforts me right now.
days.intention: Today I'll let the Prince of Peace carry what I can't.
days.higher_self: Which of your names do I need most today?
days.shadow: Where am I trying to be my own counsellor and getting tired?
days.humor: Things I've tried to govern on my own shoulders this week: a list.
days.meditation: Breathe slowly and on each breath say one name: Wonderful. Counsellor. Mighty God. Everlasting Father. Prince of Peace. Let each name sit for a full breath. Notice which one your heart leans toward. Say that name again, more slowly. Picture the weight you carry being moved from your shoulders onto stronger ones. Feel your shoulders lower. Breathe out fully. Rest in that name for five more breaths before returning to your day. Take one more slow breath, feel your feet on the floor, and when you are ready, open your eyes.
days.verse: For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.
days.faith_reflection: Which name of God feels most true to me this Christmas week?
days.faith_action: Write that name on a sticky note and put it where you'll see it.

days.gratitude: Something that grew since the New Moon on December 8.
days.intention: At this Full Moon, I celebrate ___ and release ___.
days.higher_self: What growth do you want me to notice tonight?
days.shadow: What am I holding onto that the light now shows I can let go?
days.humor: Full Moon confession: the thing I blamed on the moon that was definitely me.
days.meditation: Tonight the moon is full. If you can, look at it, or picture it rising round and bright. Breathe in and imagine its silver light filling your chest. Breathe out and let it pour over your shoulders. Name one thing that has grown this month and say, "Thank you." Name one thing you are ready to release and say, "I let it go." Picture it drifting up like a lantern. Say, "God of hope, fill me with joy and peace." Rest in the light for six breaths.
days.verse: Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost.
days.faith_reflection: Where do I need hope to overflow, not just get by?
days.faith_action: Speak one hope out loud before bed tonight.

days.gratitude: A quiet moment from this season I want to treasure.
days.intention: On Christmas Eve, I'll ponder instead of perform.
days.higher_self: What are you asking me to keep in my heart tonight?
days.shadow: What part of the holidays makes me feel I'm performing?
days.humor: Christmas Eve status: wrapping at midnight / calm and cozy / hiding in the pantry.
days.meditation: Sit somewhere quiet, even for two minutes. Breathe in and picture a stable at night: straw, cold air, the warmth of animals, a small lamp. Mary sits still, holding a newborn. She is not rushing. She is pondering. Breathe in, "Keep." Breathe out, "Ponder." Gather three moments from this year and hold them in your heart like she did. Do not explain them. Just treasure them. Sit in the stable's hush for six breaths before you rise. Take one more slow breath, feel your feet on the floor, and when you are ready, open your eyes.
days.verse: But Mary kept all these things, and pondered them in her heart.
days.faith_reflection: What from this year do I need to ponder before I move on?
days.faith_action: Write three moments to treasure on the page tonight.

days.gratitude: The best gift I received that wasn't wrapped.
days.intention: Today I'll receive joy without managing it.
days.higher_self: What does Christmas want to say to my heart today?
days.shadow: Where do I struggle to receive, even love?
days.humor: Christmas Day awards: best dressed, best napper, most suspicious gift.
days.meditation: Pause in the middle of the day, even if it's noisy. Close your eyes for a moment. Breathe in and imagine the angel's message: good tidings, great joy, to you. Let the words "for unto you" land personally. Breathe out and let your shoulders drop. Say, "A Saviour is born." Picture receiving the greatest gift with open hands, not earning it. Smile softly and let your hands rest open. Feel your feet on the floor. Take three more breaths of gratitude, then open your eyes and go enjoy your people.
days.verse: For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord.
days.faith_reflection: What does "unto you" mean to me personally this year?
days.faith_action: Tell one person today what this day means to you, simply.

days.gratitude: A moment of peace in the middle of holiday noise.
days.intention: Today I'll let peace be the referee in my heart.
days.higher_self: Where should peace rule instead of my reactions?
days.shadow: Which family pattern pulls me back into an old role?
days.humor: Leftovers I've eaten for breakfast today: a confession.
days.meditation: Sit with both feet on the floor. Breathe in for four, out for six. Picture a calm referee standing in the center of your heart, holding up a hand whenever conflict starts. Let them have authority. Breathe in, "Let peace rule." Breathe out, "Be thankful." Picture one person you love and silently thank God for them. Then one more. Then one who is hard to love. Hold peace for all three. Rest for five breaths. Take one more slow breath, feel your feet on the floor, and when you are ready, open your eyes.
days.verse: And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to the which also ye are called in one body; and be ye thankful.
days.faith_reflection: Where is peace being outvoted in my heart?
days.faith_action: Thank three people today, in person or by text.

days.gratitude: A kindness someone showed me that I never repaid.
days.intention: Today I'll be tenderhearted on purpose.
days.higher_self: Who do you want me to forgive, even a little?
days.shadow: What resentment am I keeping alive by replaying it?
days.humor: Unread texts I owe: a guilt-free amnesty list.
days.meditation: Breathe slowly and picture a stone in your hand. It is heavy and rough. This stone is a grudge. Feel its weight without blame. Breathe in and ask, "Am I ready to set this down, even partway?" If yes, imagine your fingers loosening. If no, that is fine; just notice. Breathe out and say, "Be kind, tenderhearted, forgiving." Picture yourself being forgiven too. Let warmth move into your palm where the stone was. Rest for six breaths. Take one more slow breath, feel your feet on the floor, and when you are ready, open your eyes.
days.verse: And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ’s sake hath forgiven you.
days.faith_reflection: Where has God's forgiveness of me made it easier to forgive others?
days.faith_action: Do one small kindness for someone who frustrates you.

days.gratitude: A loving moment that pushed fear out of the room.
days.intention: Today I'll let love lead over fear.
days.higher_self: What fear can love answer for me today?
days.shadow: Which fear has been driving my choices this year?
days.humor: My fear vs. my faith: a boxing match. Who won round one today?
days.meditation: Breathe in and notice where fear lives in your body, maybe your stomach, chest, or throat. Place a hand there. Breathe out slowly. Picture love entering that place like warm sunlight through a window. It doesn't fight the fear. It simply fills the room until fear has nowhere to stand. Say, "Perfect love casts out fear." Breathe with that image for eight breaths. When you open your eyes, notice one thing you can do today from love, not fear. Let one more slow breath settle all the way down to your feet.
days.verse: There is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love.
days.faith_reflection: What would I attempt if love were louder than fear?
days.faith_action: Do one small thing today you've been afraid to do.

days.gratitude: A lesson I learned this year that I'm grateful for.
days.intention: Today I'll ask for wisdom before I decide.
days.higher_self: What wisdom do you have for my next year?
days.shadow: Where do I pretend to know because asking feels weak?
days.humor: Decisions I made this year by flipping a coin, ranked by results.
days.meditation: Close your eyes and picture standing at a crossroads. Each path leads into the new year. Breathe slowly. You do not need to choose yet. Breathe in, "I ask." Breathe out, "I receive." Imagine wisdom given freely, without scolding, like a friend handing you a map. Hold the map in your mind. What is the first word you see written there? Let it come. Rest with it for six breaths, and thank God for giving liberally. Take one more slow breath, feel your feet on the floor, and when you are ready, open your eyes.
days.verse: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.
days.faith_reflection: What decision coming up needs wisdom more than willpower?
days.faith_action: Write the decision down and ask for wisdom specifically.

days.gratitude: A goodness that crowned my 2026.
days.intention: Today I'll name how this year was crowned, not just survived.
days.higher_self: What do you want me to carry into the new year?
days.shadow: What from this year am I ready to leave behind, kindly?
days.humor: 2026 in one movie title, plus the sequel I'm hoping for.
days.meditation: Sit comfortably and breathe slowly. Picture the twelve months of this year like a string of lights. Starting with January, let each month light up as you breathe in. Notice one good thing in each. Some months may glow dimmer, and that is okay. When all twelve are lit, imagine them forming a gentle crown resting on your head. Say, "Thou crownest the year with thy goodness." Feel it rest there. Breathe gratitude for six breaths before you open your eyes.
days.verse: Thou crownest the year with thy goodness; and thy paths drop fatness.
days.faith_reflection: Where did I see God's goodness most clearly this year?
days.faith_action: List one goodness from each month of 2026.
